subject: Fracture MAP: stability observatory, rebaseline request, and escalation
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Li <jordan@staxhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Fracture MAP: stability observatory, rebaseline request, and escalation

Jordan —

Quick note after this morning's sync: the evaluation plan for the Fracture pilot has drifted across three dependencies (data export, SOC/attestation window, and testbed provisioning). That combination creates a non-linear slip risk on the go-live window we previously agreed on.

I attached an updated MAP (MAP_Fracture_v3.pdf) and a short risk observatory extract below. High level:
- Current go-live target: 2026-07-30 (at risk)
- Primary blockers: export schema freeze (still open), SOC-2 evidence delivery (legal/procurement lag), and internal testbed queue (ops backfill)

Immediate asks:
1) Can Stax commit to a firm date for the export schema freeze by EOD Friday so we can lock the eval gating tests?
2) If procurement cannot accelerate SOC-2 evidence, would you accept a scoped canary for non-PHI traffic?
3) Let's schedule a 30-minute triage tomorrow to agree on a rebaseline and confirm approval runway (copying Laura/Marissa to coordinate credits / escalation).

I propose the following contingency lanes in the MAP appendix:
- Lane A (preferred): two-week export freeze and SOC evidence by 7/10 => keeps 7/30 go-live with reduced acceptance tests
- Lane B (fallback): soft-launch 8/15 with full acceptance after SOC evidence; Redwood provides a temporary support credit (TBD)

Attachments: MAP_Fracture_v3.pdf (MAP), Fracture_risk_log_Q3.xlsx (risk extract).

Thanks —
Priyom
Product Partnerships | Redwood Inference
pri yom@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0124

From: Jordan Li <jordan@staxhealth.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fracture MAP: stability observatory, rebaseline request, and escalation

Thanks, Priyom —

Appreciate the clear breakdown. Short answers:
- Export schema freeze: we can aim to freeze on Monday 2026-06-29 but I need a short checklist from your side (fields that are truly blocking the eval).
- SOC-2 evidence: procurement says they can turn over the minimal attestation package by 7/08, but full documentation will take longer.
- Canary for non-PHI traffic: yes, that's acceptable as a contingency but we'll need a narrow acceptance gate for the first two endpoints.

I can do the triage tomorrow at 11am PT. If that doesn't work I can make time after 3pm.

Jordan Li
Head of Platform Integrations, Stax Health
jordan@staxhealth.com | (617) 555-3310

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 12:20:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Fracture MAP: stability observatory, rebaseline request, and escalation

Jonas — forwarding the thread. Quick internal read: Jordan's answers are reasonable but procurement promise for 7/08 is tight. If Stax slips on the attestation we should be prepared to offer a support credit or limited SLA for the canary.

Proposed internal move:
- Approve up to 2 weeks of account credit (estimated $18k) for staged canary and engineering hours if Stax asks for a fall-back soft-launch.
- Approve a one-time procurement escalation from our side (Legal + Trust) to nudge Stax procurement; Laura can lead with their counterparty.

Action for you, Jonas: please confirm if credit authorization at the requested amount is within your tolerance or if you need me to escalate to Sales Ops. We need a yes/no before we go into triage with the customer.

--
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Subject: Fracture MAP — triage notes, agreed rebaseline, and next steps (exec summary)

Jordan / team —

Thanks for the triage today. Quick executive summary and commitments we agreed on during the call:

Decisions / rebaseline
- Export schema freeze: 2026-06-29 (Jordan will share the freeze checklist by EOD Monday)
- SOC-2 minimal attestation window: Stax procurement to deliver minimal package by 2026-07-08; full evidence to follow
- Go-live (soft canary): rebaselined to 2026-08-15 for full scope; narrow non-PHI canary to begin 2026-07-18 if attestation arrives on 7/08

Redwood commitments
- We'll open a canary environment for non-PHI traffic and provide a temporary support credit capped at $18,000 if Stax requests fallback to the 8/15 timeline (see attached Fracture_risk_log_Q3.xlsx for credit calc).
- Engineering will prioritize a small gating test harness for the export checks; ETA for harness ready: 2026-07-05.
- If Stax misses the 7/08 attestation, Redwood will provide a rollback runbook and extend the trial window by two weeks at no additional cost.

Open items
- Jordan to send the freeze-checklist by 2026-06-29 EOD (HS deal record: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/52342)
- Laura/Marissa to request procurement escalation (Redwood legal + trust contact) if evidence doesn't arrive on 7/08
- Priyom to push a DocuSign for the scoped canary amendment (link to follow)

Please reply to confirm or flag anything missing. If we don't hear objections, we'll treat this as the sanctioned rebaseline and update the MAP appendix and the risk log (attached).

Thanks again —
Priyom
Product Partnerships | Redwood Inference
